work_units.notes:
The May 12 canonical UAT loaded all 21 tables / 74,190,187 rows, then
spent most runtime in repeated scans of large JoinOrder relationship tables.
Examples from the timeout log include q6a at 46.17s, q16b at 65.3s, q17a
at 59.41s, q17e at 59.20s, and q17f at 50.55s.

SQLite now creates a JoinOrder-scoped helper index set after load, covering
the canonical JOB join keys and high-selectivity filter columns across the
large fact/relationship tables and small dimension tables. The helper path
runs only when all 21 JoinOrder tables are present, then runs `ANALYZE` so
SQLite plans against the new statistics.

Full-data local probe under `/Users/joe/Developer/benchmark_runs` loaded
21 tables / 74,190,187 rows and built 32 helper indexes in 455.322s. A
follow-up pass over all 113 canonical queries on the indexed database
passed in 200.021s total. The canonical UAT shape is 1 warmup + 3
measurement passes, so the measured estimate is roughly 455s + 4 * 200s =
1,255s plus orchestration overhead, comfortably under the 7,200s corpus
backfill budget.
